title: Structural Collapse Fire Tests: Single Story, Wood Frame Structures
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology

panel_model.thickness_basis: NISTIR 7094 identifies the roof materials as nominal 12.7 mm plywood and OSB; applying that nominal source-panel thickness to the cone samples is an inference because individual cone specimen thicknesses were not reported.
panel_model.thickness_source_location: PDF page 9 (printed page 3), cone sample relationship on PDF pages 14 and 19
panel_model.plywood_layer_thickness_assumption: Five equal-thickness plies; individual veneer and adhesive thicknesses were not reported.

material_property_profiles.source: NISTIR 4916, Controlling Moisture in the Roof Cavities of Manufactured Housing, Table 1 Heat Transfer Properties.
material_property_profiles.source_scope: Constant room-temperature roof-sheathing properties used by the NIST MOIST analysis; not measurements of the NISTIR 7094 cone specimens and not valid high-temperature reaction properties.
material_property_profiles.density_policy: Reference densities are recorded for traceability but are not applied. Each cone specimen retains its measured initial mass and mass-derived effective density.

plywood.label: Exterior-Grade Plywood
plywood.adhesive_interpretation: Four ply interfaces are recorded, but unknown glue-line geometry and resistance are not invented; the aggregate plywood conductivity is used without an extra interface penalty.

osb.label: Oriented Strand Board
osb.adhesive_interpretation: The strand-binder composite remains an aggregate one-layer material because the NISTIR 7094 binder type, content, and density profile are unreported.

temperature_dependent_heat_capacity.source: USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Wood Handbook: Wood as an Engineering Material, Chapter 4, equation 4-18a (2021 edition).
temperature_dependent_heat_capacity.source_equation: cp0 = 0.1031 + 0.003867 T kJ/(kg K), with T in K
temperature_dependent_heat_capacity.application: The published dry-wood curve is normalized at 293.15 K to preserve each NISTIR 4916 panel-specific reference cp. Only the remaining dry-wood mass uses this curve; water, char, and ash retain their existing separate heat capacities.
temperature_dependent_heat_capacity.out_of_range_policy: Clamp the equation input to 280-420 K. This avoids extrapolating the low-temperature dry-wood relation into the pyrolysis and char regimes.
temperature_dependent_heat_capacity.conductivity_policy: Keep each NISTIR 4916 panel conductivity constant. The Wood Handbook only gives an approximate 2-3 percent increase per 10 C here, without a validated cone-test temperature range for these composites.
temperature_dependent_heat_capacity.composite_limit: The curve describes wood and is not a direct high-temperature measurement of the NISTIR 7094 plywood adhesive or OSB binder composite.

secondary_tar_cracking.equation: tar -> gas; k(T) = A exp(-E / (R T)); converted fraction = 1 - exp(-k tau).
secondary_tar_cracking.model_source: NIST, Thermal Decomposition of Vegetative Fuels, Model III reaction R4 and Supplemental Table SI-4.
secondary_tar_cracking.listed_primary_source: C. Di Blasi, Analysis of convection and secondary reaction effects within porous solid fuels undergoing pyrolysis, Combustion Science and Technology 90, 315-340 (1993).
secondary_tar_cracking.residence_time_policy: One second is the nominal diagnostic scenario, not a fitted parameter; sensitivity is reported at 0.9, 1.0, and 2.2 seconds. The current solid-cell model has no gas-phase control volume or predicted char-layer residence time.
secondary_tar_cracking.out_of_range_policy: No conversion below 773 K; clamp the Arrhenius input at 1073 K above the range. These are the reported homogeneous vapor-phase cracking experiment limits, not a claimed validation range for the separate Di Blasi Model III coefficient pair.

residence_time_sensitivity.source: Boroson, Howard, Longwell, and Peters, Product yields and kinetics from the vapor phase cracking of wood pyrolysis tars, AIChE Journal 35, 120-128 (1989).
residence_time_sensitivity.feedstock: Sweet gum hardwood; approximately 2 cm deep bed; primary pyrolysis heating rate 0.2 K/s.
residence_time_sensitivity.interpretation: The endpoint residence times and the existing one-second diagnostic are applied without refitting. The experiment envelope is contextual evidence only because Boroson's distributed-activation-energy model and tar source differ from the single Di Blasi Model III branch used here.

secondary_tar_cracking.scope: Reclassify primary tar as secondary gas or surviving tar without changing total volatile mass, solid heat balance, Flow fuel source, ignition time, or mass-loss rate.
secondary_tar_cracking.validation_limit: NIST describes Model III as a literature re-examination rather than a fit to a dedicated secondary-tar experiment. Product partition is therefore diagnostic and is not used for parameter selection.

equations.residence_time_s: tau = L / u = porosity mu L^2 / (K deltaP)

gas_transport_diagnostic.source: Pozzobon et al., Radiative pyrolysis of wet wood under intermediate heat flux: experiments and modelling, Fuel Processing Technology 128, 319-330 (2014).

source_context.interpretation: Values reported in the paper's physical-properties table for its beech-sphere model. They are context only and are not assigned to the NIST plywood coupon.

gas_transport_diagnostic.policy: Expose a complete SI-unit Darcy input contract and report missing plywood state. Do not calculate residence time from beech context values or feed it into secondary-tar conversion.

char_geometry_diagnostic.source: Pozzobon et al., Radiative pyrolysis of wet wood under intermediate heat flux: experiments and modelling, Fuel Processing Technology 128, 319-330 (2014).

source_context.material: 10 mm diameter beech sphere at 9 percent initial moisture under 120 kW/m2, not plywood
source_context.interpretation: The paper reports that correcting its predicted length with the experimentally observed shrinkage factor moves the modeled front from 1.3 mm to 0.95 mm versus a 1.0 mm observation. This demonstrates that a fixed-grid reaction front and a physical shrunk thickness are distinct quantities. Its beech shrinkage is not transferred to plywood.

char_geometry_diagnostic.physical_char_layer_thickness_policy: Withhold physical char-layer thickness until a plywood shrinkage relation and a defensible front definition are available. The fixed-grid mass-equivalent depth is diagnostic only and cannot satisfy the Darcy layer-thickness input.
char_geometry_diagnostic.interpretation: Each equal-thickness panel cell contributes its dry-wood conversion fraction times its original thickness. The sum is an unshrunk mass-equivalent reaction depth, not a contiguous front location and not a physical char-layer thickness.

arrhenius_model.equation: k(T) = A exp(-E / (R T)); first-order dry-wood consumption uses 1 - exp(-k dt).
arrhenius_model.primary_source: Thurner, F. and Mann, U., Kinetic investigation of wood pyrolysis, Ind. Eng. Chem. Process Des. Dev. 20(3), 1981, DOI 10.1021/i200014a015.

parallel_product_mass_accounting.gas: Emitted primary gas; 1 kg pathway conversion produces 1 kg lumped gas.
parallel_product_mass_accounting.tar: Emitted condensable tar; 1 kg pathway conversion produces 1 kg lumped tar.
parallel_product_mass_accounting.char: Retained primary char; 1 kg pathway conversion produces 1 kg char before oxidation.

arrhenius_model.interpretation: The three published mass-basis first-order rates compete for the same unreacted dry wood. Product fractions are k_i / sum(k), not separately fitted fixed yields. A constrained common scale preserves those temperature-dependent branching ratios during calibration.

replicate_split.strategy: Fixed by sample identifier before parameter search; average SAMP.1 and SAMP.2 within each heat flux for selection, reserve SAMP.3 for validation.

holdout.relationship: Different wood product from the plywood calibration material; external-material holdout, not an in-material validation split.

adapter_assumptions.geometry: Equal exposed area and initial wet mass are mapped to a thin cylindrical coupon because the current authoritative grid is cylindrical.
adapter_assumptions.ignition_definition: First model pyrolysis-gas rate at or above 1e-6 kg/s; this is a proxy, not the report's observed sustained flaming.
adapter_assumptions.mass_loss_definition: Mean modeled release rate after proxy ignition while release remains above 1e-6 kg/s.
